Linear and generalized linear models from a formula or a numeric design. Result keys, inference, and algorithms are detailed in Model contracts; formula syntax in Model formulas.

Formula models

fit_ols()

Linear model from a formula, like R’s lm(): builds the model matrix and fits by least squares, weighted least squares when weights are given (as lm(weights = )), with offset() terms. Until phit 0.5, an array first argument (or named x:/y:) runs the deprecated matrix fit, Phit_ols_matrix(), with one E_USER_DEPRECATED; its result has no formula keys. Factor levels unused after deletion are dropped, as lm() does. Rank deficiency raises 1004 instead of R’s NA coefficients. Formula syntax and R differences: docs/formulas.qmd. Rows with null/NAN in any variable the formula uses are dropped with one E_WARNING (missing ‘raise’ rejects them); retained_rows/dropped_rows are original positions.

Phit\fit_ols(    mixed $formula = NULL,    mixed $data = NULL,    string $missing = 'drop',    mixed $weights = NULL,    ?array $offset = NULL,    bool $intercept = true,    ?array $x = NULL,    ?array $y = NULL,): array
Parameter Type Default Description
$formula mixed NULL R formula, e.g. ‘y ~ log(x) + f * z + offset(log(t))’ (deprecated until 0.5: a matrix x)
$data mixed NULL Named columns or factor descriptors; objects use toModelData(), else toColumns() (deprecated: y)
$missing string 'drop' ‘drop’ removes rows with null or NAN in any variable the model uses and warns once; ‘raise’ rejects them
$weights mixed NULL Positive prior weights aligned with the original rows, or a column name
$offset ?array NULL Deprecated matrix form only; in a formula write offset()
$intercept bool true Deprecated matrix form only; in a formula write - 1
$x ?array NULL Deprecated: use Phit_ols_matrix()
$y ?array NULL Deprecated: use Phit_ols_matrix()

Returns

array{  coefficients: list<float>,  covariance: list<list<float>>,  std_errors: list<float>,  p_values: list<float>,  conf_int: list<array{float,float}>,  fitted: list<float>,  residuals: list<float>,  log_likelihood: float,  df_residual: int,  diagnostics: array{converged:bool,solver:string,warnings:list<string>,iterations?:int,evaluations?:int,gradient_max?:float,boundary?:bool,singular?:bool},  n_input: int,  n_observations: int,  n_dropped: int,  retained_rows: list<int>,  dropped_rows: list<int>,  t_statistics: list<float>,  rss: float,  residual_variance: float,  sigma: float,  r_squared: float,  adj_r_squared: float,  formula: string,  response: string,  columns: list<string>,  terms: list<string>,  assign: list<int>,  intercept: bool,  named: array<string,float>,  predvars: array{levels:array<string,list<string>>,poly:array<string,array{alpha:list<float>,norm2:list<float>}>},}

Errors Statistical or input error (codes 1001–1008); unsupported functions/families/random terms raise 1007.

fit_generalized_linear()

Generalized linear model from a formula, like R’s glm(): gaussian/identity (the OLS core), binomial/logit, binomial/probit and poisson/log (the matrix GLM cores). Binomial responses: 0/1, logical, factor/string (first level = failure), proportions with trial weights, or cbind(successes, failures). The empty link selects the canonical link. Formula syntax and R differences: docs/formulas.qmd. Rows with null/NAN in any variable the formula uses are dropped with one E_WARNING (missing ‘raise’ rejects them); retained_rows/dropped_rows are original positions.

Phit\fit_generalized_linear(    string $formula,    mixed $data,    string $family = 'gaussian',    string $link = '',    string $missing = 'drop',    mixed $weights = NULL,): array
Parameter Type Default Description
$formula string required R formula, e.g. ‘y ~ log(x) + f * z + offset(log(t))’
$data mixed required Named columns or factor descriptors; objects use toModelData(), else toColumns()
$family string 'gaussian' ‘gaussian’, ‘binomial’ or ‘poisson’
$link string '' ’’ (canonical), ‘identity’, ‘logit’, ‘probit’ or ‘log’
$missing string 'drop' ‘drop’ removes rows with null or NAN in any variable the model uses and warns once; ‘raise’ rejects them
$weights mixed NULL Positive prior weights aligned with the original rows, or a column name

Returns

array{  coefficients: list<float>,  covariance: list<list<float>>,  std_errors: list<float>,  p_values: list<float>,  conf_int: list<array{float,float}>,  fitted: list<float>,  residuals: list<float>,  log_likelihood: float,  df_residual: int,  diagnostics: array{converged:bool,solver:string,warnings:list<string>,iterations?:int,evaluations?:int,gradient_max?:float,boundary?:bool,singular?:bool},  n_input: int,  n_observations: int,  n_dropped: int,  retained_rows: list<int>,  dropped_rows: list<int>,  z_statistics: list<float>,  deviance: float,  null_deviance: float,  aic: float,  iterations: int,  converged: bool,  family: string,  link: string,  formula: string,  response: string,  columns: list<string>,  terms: list<string>,  assign: list<int>,  intercept: bool,  named: array<string,float>,  predvars: array{levels:array<string,list<string>>,poly:array<string,array{alpha:list<float>,norm2:list<float>}>},  t_statistics?: list<float>,  rss?: float,  residual_variance?: float,  sigma?: float,  r_squared?: float,  adj_r_squared?: float,}

Errors Statistical or input error (codes 1001–1008); unsupported functions/families/random terms raise 1007.

model_matrix()

R-compatible model.matrix() for a formula over named columns: treatment contrasts (first level is the reference), contr.poly for ordered factors, R column names/term order, inline transforms, offset() and random-effect bars. Unused factor levels are kept, as in model.matrix(); x includes the “(Intercept)” column when present. Formula syntax and R differences: docs/formulas.qmd. Rows with null/NAN in any variable the formula uses are dropped with one E_WARNING (missing ‘raise’ rejects them); retained_rows/dropped_rows are original positions.

Phit\model_matrix(    string $formula,    mixed $data,    string $missing = 'drop',): array
Parameter Type Default Description
$formula string required R formula, e.g. ‘y ~ log(x) + f * z + offset(log(t))’
$data mixed required Named columns or factor descriptors; objects use toModelData(), else toColumns()
$missing string 'drop' ‘drop’ removes rows with null or NAN in any variable the model uses and warns once; ‘raise’ rejects them

Returns

array{  y: list<float>|list<array{float,float}>|null,  response_levels?: list<string>,  x: list<list<float>>,  columns: list<string>,  intercept: bool,  terms: list<string>,  assign: list<int>,  formula: string,  response: string|null,  offset: list<float>|null,  random: list<array{label:string,group:string,columns:list<string>,correlated:bool,z:list<list<float>>,groups:list<int|string>}>,  n_input: int,  n_observations: int,  n_dropped: int,  retained_rows: list<int>,  dropped_rows: list<int>,}

Errors Statistical or input error (codes 1001–1008); unsupported functions/families/random terms raise 1007.

predict()

Predictions for new data from a fit_ols (formula), fit_generalized_linear, fit_mixed_gaussian or fit_mixed_logistic result, like R’s predict(): the fit’s formula is rebuilt over newdata with the fitted factor levels and poly() basis (its predvars key). A level the fit never saw is an error. Rows with missing predictors predict null and are listed in missing_rows. type ‘response’ applies the inverse link; seFit uses the delta method on that scale. Intervals (‘confidence’ or ‘prediction’, t with df_residual) are for fit_ols fits. Mixed fits add random effects of known groups (random: false gives population predictions; allowNewLevels predicts unseen groups at zero). GLM standard errors use the covariance at the final coefficients (docs/r-compatibility.qmd).

Phit\predict(    array $fit,    mixed $newdata,    string $type = 'link',    bool $seFit = false,    string $interval = 'none',    float $level = 0.95,    bool $random = true,    bool $allowNewLevels = false,): array
Parameter Type Default Description
$fit array required A formula fit result (needs formula, coefficients, covariance, columns and predvars)
$newdata mixed required Named columns, as for the fit; the response may be absent
$type string 'link' ‘link’ (linear predictor) or ‘response’
$seFit bool false Also return standard errors of the predictions; fixed-effect fits only
$interval string 'none' ‘none’, ‘confidence’ or ‘prediction’
$level float 0.95 Confidence level of the interval
$random bool true Mixed fits: include random effects (lme4 re.form = NULL) or not (re.form = NA)
$allowNewLevels bool false Predict a group the fit never saw at the population level instead of raising 1001

Returns

array{  fit: list<float|null>,  se_fit?: list<float|null>,  df?: int,  residual_scale?: float,  lower?: list<float|null>,  upper?: list<float|null>,  level: float|null,  n_input: int,  n_predicted: int,  missing_rows: list<int>,}

Errors Input error (1001), malformed fit, new levels, or unsupported options (1007).

Matrix models

fit_ols_matrix()

Least-squares fit of a numeric design, like R’s lm.fit() with the full summary. Predictor matrix: rows are observations. A fixed intercept is prepended by default. null/NAN rows follow the missing policy; weights/offset are aligned with original rows.

Phit\fit_ols_matrix(    array $x,    array $y,    string $missing = 'drop',    ?array $weights = NULL,    ?array $offset = NULL,    bool $intercept = true,): array
Parameter Type Default Description
$x array required Predictor matrix: one row per observation and one numeric column per predictor; null or NAN is missing
$y array required Numeric response, one value per row; null or NAN is missing
$missing string 'drop' ‘drop’ removes rows with null or NAN in any variable the model uses and warns once; ‘raise’ rejects them
$weights ?array NULL Positive weights: weighted least squares, as lm(weights = )
$offset ?array NULL Known part of the linear predictor, aligned with the rows; null is zero
$intercept bool true False uses x exactly (including any caller-supplied ones).

Returns

array{  coefficients: list<float>,  covariance: list<list<float>>,  std_errors: list<float>,  p_values: list<float>,  conf_int: list<array{float,float}>,  fitted: list<float>,  residuals: list<float>,  log_likelihood: float,  df_residual: int,  diagnostics: array{converged:bool,solver:string,warnings:list<string>,iterations?:int,evaluations?:int,gradient_max?:float,boundary?:bool,singular?:bool},  n_input: int,  n_observations: int,  n_dropped: int,  retained_rows: list<int>,  dropped_rows: list<int>,  t_statistics: list<float>,  rss: float,  residual_variance: float,  sigma: float,  r_squared: float,  adj_r_squared: float,}

Errors Statistical or input error (codes 1001–1008).

See also Details

fit_logistic_matrix()

Binomial logit fit of a numeric design by Newton steps, like R’s glm(family = binomial). Predictor matrix: rows are observations. A fixed intercept is prepended by default. null/NAN rows follow the missing policy; weights/offset are aligned with original rows.

Phit\fit_logistic_matrix(    array $x,    array $y,    string $missing = 'drop',    ?array $weights = NULL,    ?array $offset = NULL,    bool $intercept = true,): array
Parameter Type Default Description
$x array required Predictor matrix: one row per observation and one numeric column per predictor; null or NAN is missing
$y array required 0/1 outcomes, or proportions with integer trial weights; null or NAN is missing
$missing string 'drop' ‘drop’ removes rows with null or NAN in any variable the model uses and warns once; ‘raise’ rejects them
$weights ?array NULL Positive integer trial counts aligned with the rows; null is one trial per row
$offset ?array NULL Known part of the linear predictor, aligned with the rows; null is zero
$intercept bool true False uses x exactly (including any caller-supplied ones).

Returns

fit_probit_matrix()

$offset ?array NULL Known part of the linear predictor, aligned with the rows; null is zero
$intercept bool true False uses x exactly (including any caller-supplied ones).
